- Overestimate prices after recent sentiment spikes (especially when sentiment is negative but model ignores it).  
- Underestimate when sentiment is consistently negative over 3+ days — model tends to ignore downward pressure.  
- Overshoot after sharp upward moves — model reacts too quickly, then corrects too late.  
- Mean-reversion bias: model holds prices too high after recent peaks, especially if sentiment is neutral or slightly negative.  
- Lag in response to sentiment shifts — model often reacts 1–2 days after sentiment changes, leading to delayed corrections.  
- Avoid overconfidence in short-term momentum — sentiment history should dampen forecast volatility, especially if sentiment is volatile or negative.
